raw.assessment: The incumbent delivered weekly bookings to eleven of twelve groups and supports telephone or desk requests with staffed key collection. Central coordination may explain this coverage, but that causal account is untested. Three conflicts and mean administration of 127.5 minutes/week miss the corresponding targets in the observed period; total need fulfillment cannot be assessed. O2 suggests unused capacity, but O5 is a concrete limitation: rooms are not interchangeable because only one has a piano, and blank equipment fields do not establish piano independence. Aggregate vacancy therefore does not establish usable availability. Late starts also do not establish safely reclaimable sessions.

openings.claim: Inherited times and uniform 90-minute reservations may conceal feasible allocations, but equipment and acceptable-window constraints may instead explain the unmet requests.
openings.delta: Distinguish recoverable scheduling mismatch from scarcity of usable room-time, rather than treating all vacant hours as substitutes.
openings.prediction: If scheduling mismatch matters, a candidate allocation using confirmed windows, durations and equipment needs will satisfy more stated needs than inherited reservations while retaining every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. If piano-compatible or evening capacity binds, deficits will persist in those specific combinations despite overall vacancy.
openings.probe: Use the twelve short contact conversations to record total weekly needs, acceptable windows, necessary equipment and whether shorter sessions are usable; record outside rehearsals separately. Compare the current schedule with a paper candidate inside existing hours, fixing both performances and allocating requested weekly minimums before additional time. Identify infeasibility explicitly; confirm changes before adoption and measure fulfillment over eight weeks.
assumptions: Contacts can report reliable group requirements.
Shorter bookings satisfy needs only where groups confirm this.

openings.claim: A numbered desk master record with explicit confirmation of each reservation change may reduce conflicting expectations and reconciliation work.
openings.delta: Treat a change as one recorded transaction communicated through existing channels, with the online copy visibly dated to its last synchronization.
openings.prediction: Calendar-disagreement conflicts should decrease if divergent records are causal. Continued duplicate arrivals despite matching records and confirmed changes would instead implicate misunderstanding or another unmeasured cause; administration may rise if transaction overhead exceeds reconciliation savings.
openings.probe: Pilot desk and telephone confirmation against the master without changing slot entitlements. Log conflicts, their record/confirmation history and total administration minutes weekly, including copying and calls; evaluate fewer than two conflicts and at most 120 mean weekly minutes across eight weeks.
assumptions: Desk staff and volunteer can consult the same master during bookings and key collection.
The causes of the two duplicate-expectation incidents are unknown.

raw.assessment: Unused booked time and declined requests coexist, but neither suitable spare capacity nor flexible demand is established. One speculative capability merits a bounded test; the eight-week success target remains unproven.

openings.claim: A rehearsal obligation could retain a predictable confirmed slot while participating in a coordinated exchange of several groups’ room-times, potentially opening a suitable slot that no isolated booking change can release.
openings.delta: Replace inherited individual reservations with consented exchange cycles evaluated against actual rehearsal requirements. The speculative capability is to find and complete such cycles without increasing the volunteer’s workload.
openings.prediction: At least one unmet request can be accommodated through a fully accepted exchange cycle while every affected group retains its requested duration, required equipment and acceptable window. If no cycle exists after requirements are recorded, this capability offers no demonstrated gain for these requests.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record weekly rehearsal needs, acceptable windows, equipment and willingness to exchange. On paper, seek one cycle, preserving every requested weekly 60-minute minimum and the booked performances within existing rooms and staffed hours. Keep original reservations until all affected contacts consent by phone or in person; use one authoritative desk record and confirmed updates to its copy. Pilot one accepted cycle and record usable rehearsal time, access conflicts and all administration minutes. Compare feasibility against simply assigning currently free slots; reject the claimed exchange benefit if free-slot assignment achieves the same result. Continue evaluation over eight weeks before claiming the stated success measure.
assumptions: Useful exchange cycles exist; aggregate vacancy alone does not establish this.
Dependencies include accurate group requirements, consent, coordinated calendar updates and reliable communication.
The presently testable partial capability is finding and completing one cycle manually; routine operation within two administration hours weekly is unproven.

openings.claim: Inherited times and 90-minute slots may hide feasible allocations; equipment or window scarcity may instead bind.
openings.discriminator: Requirement-based allocation improves fulfillment, or specific piano/evening deficits persist despite vacancy.
openings.fit: Preserve C1-C4; shorter sessions require confirmation.
openings.probe: Interview twelve contacts for total needs, windows, equipment, usable durations and outside rehearsals. Compare current and paper schedules; allocate weekly minimums first, fix performances, identify infeasibility and confirm changes.
openings.uncertainty: Requirements may be unreliable; vacancy and lateness establish neither usable capacity nor safe reclamation.

openings.claim: A numbered desk master, confirmed changes and dated online copy may reduce divergent expectations and reconciliation.
openings.discriminator: Record-related conflicts fall; duplicate arrivals despite matching confirmations suggest other causes. Overhead may exceed savings.
openings.probe: Pilot shared-master booking/key collection and confirmation; log conflict histories and all copying/call minutes weekly.
openings.uncertainty: Shared-master accessibility and causes of two duplicate arrivals remain unverified.

openings.claim: Consented multi-group exchange cycles may unlock suitable time unavailable through isolated changes.
openings.discriminator: One fully accepted cycle satisfies an unmet request beyond what free-slot assignment achieves.
openings.fit: Preserve C1-C4 and affected groups' durations, equipment and windows.
openings.probe: Record exchange willingness; seek one paper cycle. Retain originals until unanimous phone/in-person consent, then confirm master/copy updates. Pilot and count usable time, conflicts and all administration.
openings.uncertainty: Useful cycles, reliable coordination and routine operation within two weekly administration hours are unproven.

lineage.reason: Exchange dependencies and incremental benefit remain distinct.

post_distill.decision: Establish requirements, compare allocations and free slots, then test any qualifying cycle alongside record confirmation. Claim success only after eight weeks show at least 90% need fulfillment, fewer than two conflicts and mean administration at most 120 minutes/week.
